title: Proof of the Derivative of Tangent Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Prove that d/dx[tan x] = sec^2(x) using the quotient identity tan(x) = sin(x)/cos(x).

steps.title: Apply Quotient Rule to sin(x)/cos(x)
steps.mathExpression: \frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right] = \frac{(\cos x)(\cos x) - (\sin x)(-\sin x)}{\cos^2 x}
steps.explanation: Numerator derivative is cos(x); denominator derivative is -sin(x).

steps.title: Simplify Numerator via Pythagorean Identity
steps.explanation: Apply cos^2(x) + sin^2(x) = 1 and reciprocal identity 1/cos(x) = sec(x).
